en: I / You / We / They + 동사원형
kr: 예: I eat, You study, They go

en: She / He / It + 동사 + s/es
부정문: don't / doesn't + 동사원형
kr: 예: I don't eat, She doesn't eat

en: 의문문: Do/Does + 주어 + 동사원형?
kr: 예: Do you study? Does she eat?

en: 의문사: What / Why / When + Do/Does + 주어 + 동사원형?
현재형은 '습관·사실·일반적 진리'를 말할 때 씁니다
kr: I work at a bank. / Water boils at 100°C.

en: 단축형(줄임말)이 실제 회화의 기본
kr: I don't = I do not, She doesn't = she does not

en: A 소리: 입을 크게 벌린 '애' — apple, at, and, cat
발음은 '입 모양 먼저, 소리는 따라온다'
kr: 거울 보고 입 모양 확인하며 연습

en: a + 자음 소리로 시작: a book, a car, a coffee
an + 모음 소리로 시작: an apple, an hour, an electronic shaver
the: 서로 아는 '바로 그것'
kr: 예: the book (방금 말한 그 책)

en: the는 '말한 적 없어도 누가 봐도 명확한 것'에도 쓴다
kr: Close the door. / Pass me the salt.

en: to + 동사원형 = ~하기 위해서 (목적)
kr: I went to Hi-Mart to buy a shaver.

en: 규칙 동사: 동사 + -ed (worked, played, studied)
불규칙 동사: 통째로 바뀜 (ate, drank, went, saw)
과거 부정문: didn't + 동사원형
과거 의문문: Did + 주어 + 동사원형?
be동사 과거형: was / were
kr: I was tired. / They were busy.

en: I'm grateful to + 사람 (+ for ~)
I'm grateful for + 명사/동명사(-ing)
여기서 to는 '전치사' → 뒤에 명사 또는 동사+ing
looking forward to + 명사
kr: the weekend, your reply, the trip

en: looking forward to + 동사ing
시간 표현: on the weekend / on Saturday
can't wait to + 동사원형 — '기대돼서 못 기다리겠다'
kr: I can't wait to see you!

en: look forward to + N/-ing 의 반대 — dread + N/-ing (싫어서 걱정되다)
kr: I dread going to the dentist.

en: F: 윗니로 아랫입술을 살짝 물고 바람 — food, fat, coffee
I(짧은 이): '이'와 '에'의 중간 — is, sit, this
Can I get a cappuccino? / I'll have an Americano.
사이즈·온도: Medium / Hot / Iced, please
옵션: Just milk, no sugar / Extra shot, please
How have you been? — 그동안 어떻게 지냈어?
sleep in — (일부러) 늦잠 자다
kr: I'm looking forward to sleeping in.

en: binge-watch — 정주행하다
improve — (실력이) 늘다, 나아지다
I'm going to + 동사원형 → 실제 발음은 'I'm gonna ~'
의문문: be동사를 주어 앞으로 — Are you gonna ~?
부정문: be동사 + not — I'm not gonna ~
kr: I'm not gonna eat. (안 먹을 거야)

en: 의문사 결합: What/Where/When/How + are you gonna ~?
kr: What are you gonna do? (뭐 할 거야?)

en: 요일·주말 앞에는 항상 on — on Sunday
will vs be going to — 뉘앙스 비교
kr: I will help you. (즉석 제안) / I'm going to visit Jeju. (이미 정함)

en: gonna는 글에는 안 쓰고 말할 때만 — 격식 차릴 땐 going to
kr: 문자/이메일엔 going to, 친구와 말할 땐 gonna

en: r: 혀를 입천장 어디에도 안 닿게 — 과장해서 굴려요
kr: study에 r 소리가 섞이지 않게 주의

en: F는 바람, G는 혀 뒷부분, L은 초성/받침 위치가 다름
I(짧은 이): 앞혀 내리고 '에/이' 중간 — is는 '에즈'에 가깝게
문장 끝 억양: 평서문은 내려요 (drink 같은 끝맺음 올리지 않기)
am / is / are + 동사ing
kr: 예: I am studying English now.

en: 진행형 의문문: What are you doing?
현재형 vs 진행형 — 평소 vs 지금
kr: I study English (평소) ↔ I am studying English (지금)

en: right now / at the moment — '지금 당장'을 강조하는 표현
kr: I'm working right now, can I call you back?

en: be going to + 동사원형 = ~할 예정 (이미 정한 계획)
kr: I am going to meet my friend tomorrow.

en: will + 동사원형 = ~할게/~할 거야 (즉석 결정·예측)
정리: 계획=going to, 즉흥=will
현재진행형으로 가까운 미래 약속 말하기
kr: I'm meeting my friend tomorrow. (이미 약속이 잡혀 있음)

en: always(100%) > usually > often > sometimes > rarely > never(0%)
위치: be동사 뒤 / 일반동사 앞
kr: I am always busy. / I usually wake up at 7.

en: never는 그 자체가 부정 — don't와 같이 쓰지 않음
kr: I never drink ✓ / I don't never ❌

en: every day / every week 도 빈도를 말한다
kr: I go to the gym every other day. (이틀에 한 번)

en: How often do you + 동사원형?
횟수 답: once / twice / three times + a day(week, month)
kr: 하루에 한 번 / 일주일에 두 번

en: hardly ever — '거의 안 한다' (rarely와 비슷)
kr: I hardly ever eat fast food.

en: A table for two, please. — 두 명 자리 부탁해요
I'd like the pasta, please. — 파스타로 할게요
What do you recommend? — 추천 메뉴가 뭐예요?
Are you ready to order? — 점원이 주문 받을 때 묻는 말
kr: Yes, I'm ready. / Can we have a few more minutes?

en: Could I get some water? — 물 좀 주시겠어요?
Can we get the bill, please? — 계산서 주세요
It was delicious! — 정말 맛있었어요!
How would you like that cooked? — 굽기 정도 묻기
Hello! / Hi! / Good morning!
Nice to meet you.
How are you? — I'm good, thanks. And you?
My name is... / I'm...
I'm from Seoul, Korea.
I like / enjoy + 동사ing
Hello! Nice to meet you.
My name is Taehyun. I'm from Seoul.
I like watching movies.
Good morning! How are you today?
It was nice meeting you. See you soon!
I enjoy cooking and listening to music.
kr: 저는 요리하고 음악 듣는 걸 좋아해요.

en: Hi! I don't think we've met. I'm Mina.
kr: 안녕하세요! 저희 처음 뵙죠. 저는 미나예요.

en: Nice to meet you, Mina. I'm Daniel.
Nice to meet you too. Where are you from?
I'm from Canada. How about you?
I'm from Seoul, Korea.
Oh, nice! What do you do?
I'm a student. I like watching movies in my free time.
kr: 저는 학생이에요. 여가 시간엔 영화 보는 걸 좋아해요.

en: That sounds fun. I enjoy hiking on weekends.
Cool! It was nice talking with you.
It was nice meeting you too, Mina.
thirteen(13) vs thirty(30) — 강세가 핵심
I am thirty years old.
What time is it? — It's three thirty.
What day is it today? — It's Friday.
My birthday is on May 5th.
What time is it? It's three thirty.
My birthday is on May 5th.
I am thirty years old.
The meeting starts at nine fifteen.
What day is it today? It's Wednesday.
Her birthday is on June 1st.
Are you free this week?
Yes. What day did you have in mind?
How about Friday? What time works for you?
Three thirty sounds good.
Great. Let's meet at the cafe on Friday at three thirty.
By the way, when is your birthday?
It's on May 5th. I'll be thirty years old.
Oh, that's next month! We should celebrate.
Sounds great. See you on Friday, then.
See you then!
a + 자음 소리: a book / an + 모음 소리: an apple
the: 서로 아는 특정한 것
복수형: books, apples / -es: boxes, watches
my / your / his / her / our / their + 명사
I have a book and an apple.
kr: 나는 책 한 권과 사과 하나가 있다.

en: Please close the door.
This is my bag. Her name is Suji.
kr: 이것은 내 가방이야. 그녀의 이름은 수지야.

en: I need a pen and an eraser.
The sun is very bright today.
Their children are very smart.
Can you close the door, please?
Sure. Is this your bag on the desk?
kr: 그럴게요. 책상 위에 있는 게 당신 가방인가요?

en: Yes, that's my bag. I have an apple inside.
kr: 네, 제 가방이에요. 안에 사과가 하나 있어요.

en: I see two books here too. Are they yours?
kr: 여기 책 두 권도 보이네요. 당신 거예요?

en: One is mine, and the other is my sister's.
kr: 하나는 제 거고, 다른 하나는 여동생 거예요.

en: What's her name?
Her name is Yuna. She's very kind.
Nice. Should I put the books on the shelf?
Yes, please. Thank you for your help.
No problem at all!
I am / You are / He·She·It is / We·They are
뒤에 명사·형용사: I am a student / I am tired
부정: I'm not / isn't / aren't
의문: Are you...? Is she...? — Yes, I am / No, she isn't
I am a student. She is a doctor.
They are not busy today.
Are you tired? — Yes, I am.
We are not ready yet.
Is he a teacher? — Yes, he is.
I'm happy, but I'm a little tired.
Hi! Are you busy right now?
No, I'm not busy. I'm free today.
kr: 아니, 안 바빠. 오늘은 시간 있어.

en: Are you tired? You look a bit sleepy.
Yes, I am. I'm tired, but I'm okay.
Is your sister a student too?
No, she isn't. She's a nurse.
That's a great job. Is she happy with it?
Yes, she is. She's very kind, too.
Nice. Are we still meeting tomorrow?
kr: 좋네. 우리 내일 만나는 거 맞지?

en: Yes, we are! See you then.
mother / father / sister / brother / parents
There are four people in my family.
He is tall / short / funny / kind
She has brown eyes / long hair
He looks like his father.
There are four people in my family.
My sister is funny. She has long hair.
He looks like his father.
My brother is short, but he is very strong.
kr: 제 형은 키가 작지만 매우 힘이 세요.

You look like your mother.
Is this a photo of your family?
Yes! There are four people in my family.
Who is this tall man?
That's my father. He's tall and very funny.
kr: 저희 아버지예요. 키가 크고 정말 재밌으세요.

en: And who does he look like?
I look like my father, actually.
I see it! Does your mother have long hair?
kr: 그런 것 같아요! 어머니는 머리가 기신가요?

en: Yes, she has long, dark hair. She's very kind.
kr: 네, 길고 검은 머리예요. 정말 친절하세요.

Thank you! I'll introduce you someday.
I have been to Japan. — 가 본 적 있다 (경험)
Have you ever eaten kimchi?

I haven't watched it yet.

I have been to Japan. (완료 — 경험 자체)
I have been to Japan twice.
kr: 나는 일본에 두 번 가 봤다.

en: Have you ever eaten Korean BBQ?
kr: 한국식 바비큐 먹어 본 적 있어?

en: I haven't finished my homework yet.
She has already left for the airport.
Have you ever been to Europe?
I went to Tokyo in 2019.
Have you ever traveled abroad?

en: Yes, I have. I've been to Japan twice.
kr: 네, 있어요. 일본에 두 번 가 봤어요.

en: When did you go there?
I went there in 2022 and last year.
Have you tried Japanese food yet?
Of course! I've already tried ramen and sushi.
Sounds amazing. I haven't been there yet.
kr: 멋지네요. 저는 아직 거기 안 가 봤어요.

en: You should go. Have you booked your trip?
Not yet, but I will soon.
Let me know if you need any tips!
짧은 단어 + er: bigger, faster + than
긴 단어: more + 형용사
as + 형용사 + as: 만큼 ~하다
kr: He is as tall as me

en: the + est / the most + 형용사
Seoul is bigger than Busan.
This is the best restaurant in town.
English is more interesting than I thought.
This phone is more expensive than that one.
He runs as fast as a professional athlete.
Today is the worst day of my week.
kr: 오늘은 제 한 주 중 최악의 날이에요.

en: Which restaurant is better, this one or that one?
kr: 이 식당이랑 저 식당 중 어디가 더 나아요?

en: I think this one is better than that one.
kr: 이 식당이 저기보다 더 나은 것 같아요.

en: Is it more expensive too?
Not really. It's about as cheap as the other one.
What's the best dish here?
The pasta is the most popular dish.
Is it spicier than the soup?
Yes, much spicier. But it's the tastiest thing on the menu.
kr: 네, 훨씬 매워요. 하지만 메뉴 중 가장 맛있어요.

en: Great, let's order the pasta then.
Good choice!
can: 능력/허락 — I can swim.
Could you...?: 정중한 요청
should: 조언 — You should get some rest.
must: 의무 — I must go now.
might: 추측 — It might rain tomorrow.
Could you open the window, please?
You should get some rest.
It might rain tomorrow.
You must wear a seatbelt in the car.
Could you pass me the salt, please?
She might be at home right now.
Could you tell me what's wrong, doctor?
kr: 선생님, 무슨 문제인지 말씀해 주실 수 있나요?

en: You should get more rest. You look very tired.
kr: 더 쉬셔야 해요. 많이 피곤해 보이세요.

en: I see. Must I take medicine every day?
Yes, you must take it twice a day.
kr: 네, 하루에 두 번 드셔야 해요.

en: Could I exercise this week?
You shouldn't exercise too hard for now.
kr: 지금은 너무 무리해서 운동하지 않는 게 좋아요.

en: It might be hard to stay still all week.
kr: 일주일 내내 가만히 있는 게 힘들 것 같아요.

en: I understand, but you must take care of your health.
kr: 이해해요, 하지만 건강을 꼭 챙기셔야 해요.

en: Could you write that down for me?
Of course. Here you go.
Excuse me, where is the station?
How far is it from here?
How long does it take?
Turn left / right at the corner.
Go straight for two blocks.
Take subway line two to City Hall.

Turn left and go straight for two blocks.
Could you tell me how to get to the museum?
kr: 박물관까지 가는 길 좀 알려주실 수 있나요?

It takes about fifteen minutes by bus.
Excuse me, how do I get to City Hall from here?
You can take subway line two. It's not far.
How long does it take by subway?
It takes about ten minutes.
Is it within walking distance too?
kr: 걸어서 갈 수 있는 거리도 되나요?

en: Yes, actually. Go straight for two blocks, then turn left.
kr: 네, 사실 가능해요. 두 블록 직진하고 좌회전하세요.

en: And then?
Turn right at the traffic lights. You'll see it on your left.
Great, thank you so much!
No problem. Have a nice walk!
I think it's a good idea.
In my opinion, English is important.
As far as I know, ...
I agree with you. / I totally agree.
I'm sorry, but I disagree.
That makes sense, but...
I think it's a good idea.
In my opinion, breakfast is the most important meal.
kr: 제 생각엔 아침이 가장 중요한 식사예요.

en: I'm sorry, but I disagree.
As far as I know, the store closes at nine.
That's a good point, however, I see it differently.
I totally agree with your opinion.
In my opinion, mornings are the best time to work.
kr: 제 생각에는 아침이 일하기 가장 좋은 시간이에요.

en: I'm sorry, but I disagree. I feel more focused at night.
kr: 미안하지만 동의하지 않아요. 저는 밤에 더 집중이 잘돼요.

en: That makes sense, but mornings are quieter, don't you think?
kr: 일리 있지만, 아침이 더 조용하지 않나요?

en: As far as I know, it depends on the person.
kr: 제가 알기로는 사람마다 다른 것 같아요.

en: I think you're right about that.
I believe sleep schedule matters more than the time itself.
kr: 저는 시간 자체보다 수면 패턴이 더 중요하다고 믿어요.

en: That's a good point, however, I still prefer mornings.
kr: 좋은 지적이지만, 그래도 저는 아침이 더 좋아요.

en: Fair enough! Everyone has their own rhythm.
kr: 그럴 수 있죠! 사람마다 리듬이 다르니까요.

en: Totally agree with that.

kr: 좋은 대화였어요. 이건 서로 다르게 생각하는 걸로 해두죠.

en: If + 현재, will: If it rains, I will stay home.

kr: 돈이 더 있다면 여행 갈 텐데

en: If I were you, I wouldn't buy it.
If + had p.p., would have p.p.: If I had known, I would have gone.
If I were you, I wouldn't buy it.
kr: 내가 너라면 그거 안 살 거야.

en: If I had more money, I would travel around the world.
kr: 돈이 더 있다면 세계여행을 할 텐데.

kr: 차가 있다면 해변으로 운전해 갈 텐데.

kr: 내가 당신이라면 먼저 집을 살 거예요.

kr: 내일 비가 오면 그래도 등산 갈 거예요?

kr: 아니요, 비가 오면 집에서 영화 볼 거예요.

kr: 더 일찍 확인했더라면 여기 갇혀있지 않았을 텐데.

en: True. Let's wait for the rain to stop.

행위자가 불명확하거나 중요하지 않을 때

en: 대상을 강조하고 싶을 때
kr: Hangul was invented by King Sejong

en: This car was made in Korea.
My wallet was stolen on the subway.
Hangul was invented by King Sejong.
The bridge was built in 1990.
The new policy will be announced tomorrow.
English is spoken all over the world.

kr: 실례합니다, 제 가방을 도난당한 것 같아요.

en: I'm sorry to hear that. When was it taken?

Yes, my passport was inside the bag.
kr: 네, 가방 안에 제 여권이 있었어요.

en: Don't worry. A report will be filed right now.

en: How long will it take to be processed?
It should be completed within a day.
Thank you. I really appreciate your help.
You're welcome. We'll contact you soon.
She said (that) she was busy.

They asked if I could come.
She said that she was busy.
The doctor told me to rest.
They asked if I could come to the party.
kr: 그들은 내가 파티에 올 수 있는지 물었다.

kr: 확인해볼게요... 네, 창가 자리 있습니다. 짐은 몇 개 부치시나요?

en: Just one suitcase. It might be a little over the weight limit, though.
kr: 캐리어 하나요. 그런데 무게 제한을 조금 넘을 수도 있어요.

en: Let's weigh it. ...It's 24 kilos, so you're fine. Here's your boarding pass.
Great, thank you. Which gate should I go to?
kr: 좋아요, 감사합니다. 어느 게이트로 가야 하나요?

en: Gate 22. Boarding starts at 10:40, so please be there by 10:20.
Got it. Is there anything else I need to do before security?
kr: 알겠습니다. 보안 검색 전에 더 해야 할 게 있을까요?

en: No, that's everything. Just have your boarding pass and ID ready at security.
kr: 아니요, 다 끝났습니다. 보안 검색대에서 탑승권과 신분증만 준비해 주세요.

en: Perfect. Thanks so much for your help!
Welcome! Do you have a reservation with us?
Yes, under the name Kim. I booked a double room for two nights.
Let me pull that up... Found it. Could I get your ID and a credit card for the deposit?
kr: 확인해볼게요... 찾았습니다. 보증금용으로 신분증과 신용카드 부탁드릴게요.

en: Of course. Also, is breakfast included in the room rate?
kr: 물론이죠. 그리고 조식이 숙박비에 포함되어 있나요?

en: Yes, it's included from 7 to 10 a.m. on the second floor.
Sounds good. What time is checkout?
Checkout is at 11 a.m. Your room is 512, on the fifth floor.
Great. Is the Wi-Fi password in the room?
Yes, it's on a card by the desk. Here are your key cards. Enjoy your stay!
kr: 네, 책상 옆 카드에 있어요. 키카드 드릴게요. 좋은 시간 보내세요!

en: Thank you very much!
Thanks for coming in today. Could you tell me a bit about yourself?
kr: 오늘 와 주셔서 감사합니다. 본인 소개를 좀 해주시겠어요?

en: Sure. I've been working in marketing for three years, mostly on social media campaigns.
kr: 네. 마케팅 분야에서 3년 정도 일했고, 주로 소셜미디어 캠페인을 맡았습니다.

en: That's great. What would you say is your biggest strength?
kr: 좋네요. 본인의 가장 큰 강점은 무엇이라고 생각하세요?

en: I think it's my ability to manage multiple projects without losing attention to detail.
kr: 여러 프로젝트를 동시에 진행하면서도 세부사항을 놓치지 않는 능력이라고 생각합니다.

en: Good to know. Why are you interested in this position specifically?
kr: 알겠습니다. 특히 이 직무에 관심을 갖게 된 이유는 무엇인가요?

en: I really admire your company's recent campaigns, and I'd love to contribute fresh ideas.
kr: 이 회사의 최근 캠페인들이 인상적이었고, 새로운 아이디어로 기여하고 싶습니다.

en: Do you have any questions for us?
Yes, what does a typical week look like for someone in this role?
kr: 네, 이 직무를 맡으면 일주일이 보통 어떻게 흘러가나요?

en: It's a mix of planning meetings and hands-on campaign work. We'll follow up by email this week.
kr: 기획 회의와 실무 작업이 섞여 있어요. 이번 주 안에 이메일로 다시 연락드릴게요.

en: That sounds great. Thank you so much for your time.
Hi, what brings you in today?
I've had a sore throat and a slight fever since yesterday.
kr: 어제부터 목이 아프고 미열이 좀 있어요.

en: I see. Any coughing or trouble swallowing?
kr: 그렇군요. 기침이나 삼키기 힘든 증상도 있나요?

en: A little coughing, and swallowing is a bit painful.
kr: 기침은 조금 있고, 삼킬 때 약간 아파요.

en: Let me take a look at your throat. ...It's a bit red. I think it's a viral infection.
kr: 목을 좀 볼게요... 약간 빨갛네요. 바이러스성 감염인 것 같아요.

en: Do I need antibiotics?
Not for now. Rest, drink warm fluids, and take this medicine for the fever.
kr: 지금은 필요 없어요. 쉬시고 따뜻한 음료를 드시고, 이 약은 열에 드세요.

en: How long should I take it?
Three times a day for five days. Come back if it gets worse or doesn't improve.
kr: 하루 세 번, 5일간이요. 더 심해지거나 나아지지 않으면 다시 오세요.

en: Okay, thank you, doctor.
Hi, let me know if you need any help finding something.
kr: 안녕하세요, 찾으시는 게 있으면 말씀해 주세요.

en: Thanks. I'm looking for a jacket for fall, something casual.
kr: 감사합니다. 가을용 캐주얼한 재킷을 찾고 있어요.

en: We have some nice ones over here. What size do you usually wear?
kr: 이쪽에 좋은 게 있어요. 보통 어떤 사이즈를 입으세요?

en: Medium, usually. Could I try this gray one on?
kr: 보통 미디엄이에요. 이 회색 한번 입어볼 수 있을까요?

en: Of course, the fitting rooms are right there. How does it fit?
kr: 물론이죠, 피팅룸이 바로 저기예요. 어떻게 맞으세요?

en: It's a little tight in the shoulders. Do you have a large?
kr: 어깨가 좀 끼네요. 라지 사이즈 있나요?

en: Let me check the stock... Yes, here's a large. Try this one.
kr: 재고 확인해볼게요... 네, 라지 있습니다. 이거 입어보세요.

en: Much better. I'll take this one. Is it on sale?
kr: 훨씬 낫네요. 이걸로 할게요. 세일하는 건가요?

en: Yes, 20% off this week. That'll be $48 at the register.
Great, I'll go pay now. Thanks for your help!
kr: 좋네요, 지금 계산하러 갈게요. 도와주셔서 감사해요!

en: Where to?
To the Grand Hotel downtown, please. Do you know it?
Yes, I know it well. It'll take about twenty minutes with this traffic.
kr: 네, 잘 알아요. 지금 교통 상황이면 20분쯤 걸릴 거예요.

en: That's fine. Could you take the highway if it's faster?
Sure, the highway should save us some time today.
kr: 네, 오늘은 고속도로가 시간을 절약해줄 거예요.

en: Perfect. Could you turn up the AC a bit? It's pretty warm.
kr: 좋아요. 에어컨 좀 더 세게 틀어주실 수 있나요? 꽤 더워서요.

en: No problem at all. Let me know if it's too cold.
kr: 전혀 문제없어요. 너무 차가우면 말씀해 주세요.

en: It's good now, thanks. How much will the fare be roughly?
kr: 지금 딱 좋아요, 감사해요. 요금은 대략 얼마나 나올까요?

en: Probably around fifteen dollars with the meter running.
kr: 미터기로 보면 대략 15달러쯽 나올 것 같아요.

en: Sounds good. We're here — keep the change.
kr: 좋아요. 다 왔네요 — 잔돈은 그냥 가지세요.

en: Hi, how can I help you today?
I'd like to open a new savings account, please.
Sure, I just need your ID and proof of address. Do you have those with you?
kr: 네, 신분증과 주소 증명서가 필요해요. 지금 가지고 계신가요?

en: Yes, here's my ID. Will a utility bill work as proof of address?
kr: 네, 신분증이요. 공공요금 청구서도 주소 증명으로 되나요?

en: Yes, that works perfectly. What's the initial deposit you'd like to make?
kr: 네, 그거면 충분해요. 초기 예치금은 얼마로 하시겠어요?

en: Let's start with $200. What's the interest rate on this account?
It's currently 2.5% annually, calculated monthly.
That sounds reasonable. Can I also get a debit card for this account?
kr: 괜찮네요. 이 계좌로 체크카드도 받을 수 있나요?

en: Of course, it'll arrive by mail in about a week.
kr: 물론이죠, 약 일주일 안에 우편으로 도착할 거예요.

en: Perfect, thank you for your help.
Hello, thanks for calling Olive Garden, how can I help you?
Hi, I'd like to make a reservation for this Saturday evening.
kr: 안녕하세요, 이번 주 토요일 저녁에 예약하고 싶어요.

en: Sure, what time were you thinking, and for how many people?
kr: 네, 몇 시쯔에 몇 분이서 오실 예정이세요?

en: Around 7 p.m., for four people.
Let me check... We have a table available at 7. Could I get your name and a phone number?
kr: 확인해볼게요... 7시에 자리 있습니다. 이름과 전화번호 알려주시겠어요?

en: It's Sarah Lee, and my number is 555-0192.
Got it. Do you have any seating preference, like a window seat?
kr: 네, 알겠습니다. 자리 선호하시는 게 있나요, 창가 자리 같이?

en: A window seat would be great if possible.
kr: 가능하면 창가 자리가 좋을 것 같아요.

en: I'll note that down. We'll see you and your party at 7 on Saturday.
Thank you so much. See you then!
Hi, thanks for coming. This is the apartment you saw online.
kr: 안녕하세요, 와주셔서 감사합니다. 온라인에서 보신 그 아파트예요.

en: It looks bigger than in the photos. How old is the building?
kr: 사진보다 더 넓어 보이네요. 건물은 얼마나 됐나요?

en: It was built about ten years ago, and renovated last year.
kr: 지은 지 10년 정도 됐고, 작년에 리모델링했어요.

en: That's good to know. Is the rent negotiable?
A little, depending on the lease length. A one-year lease gets a small discount.
kr: 계약 기간에 따라 조금은 가능해요. 1년 계약이면 약간 할인돼요.

en: I see. Are utilities included in the rent?
Water is included, but electricity and gas are separate.
Got it. Is parking available for tenants?
Yes, there's one free parking spot per unit in the basement.
kr: 네, 지하에 세대당 무료 주차 한 자리가 제공돼요.

en: That's great. I'm really interested — what's the next step?
kr: 좋네요. 정말 마음에 들어요 — 다음 절차는 어떻게 되나요?

en: Thanks for calling tech support, how can I help you today?
Hi, my internet has been disconnecting every few minutes since this morning.
kr: 안녕하세요, 오늘 아침부터 인터넷이 몇 분마다 끊겨요.

en: I'm sorry to hear that. Could you tell me the model of your router?
kr: 불편을 드려 죄송합니다. 사용 중인 라우터 모델을 알려주시겠어요?

en: It's a TP-Link, I think the model is Archer C6.
kr: TP-Link인데, 모델은 Archer C6인 것 같아요.

en: Thanks. Let's try restarting it. Could you unplug it for ten seconds and plug it back in?
kr: 감사합니다. 재시작해볼게요. 10초간 플러그를 뽑고 다시 꽂아주시겠어요?

en: Okay, I just did that. It's restarting now.
kr: 네, 방금 했어요. 지금 재시작되고 있어요.

en: Great. Once the lights are stable, try connecting again and let me know how it goes.
kr: 좋아요. 불빛이 안정되면 다시 연결해보시고 어떻게 되는지 알려주세요.

en: It seems to be working better now, but I'm not totally sure yet.
kr: 지금은 좀 더 잘 되는 것 같은데, 아직 확실하진 않아요.

en: Let's monitor it for a few minutes. If it disconnects again, we'll schedule a technician visit.
kr: 몇 분 더 지켜볼게요. 또 끊기면 기사님 방문을 잡아드릴게요.

en: Sounds good, thank you for your patience.
Excuse me, could you tell me how to get to the nearest subway station?
kr: 실례지만, 가까운 지하철역 가는 길 좀 알려주실 수 있나요?

en: Sure, go straight for two blocks and turn left at the bakery.
kr: 네, 두 블록 직진하시고 빵집에서 좌회전하세요.

en: Two blocks, then left at the bakery. Is it far from there?
kr: 두 블록, 그다음 빵집에서 좌회전이요. 거기서 멀까요?

en: Not at all, you'll see the entrance right after you turn.
kr: 전혀 아니에요, 돌면 바로 입구가 보일 거예요.

en: Great. Do you know which line goes downtown from there?
kr: 좋네요. 거기서 시내로 가는 노선이 뭔지 아시나요?

en: I think it's the green line, but check the signs to be sure.
kr: 초록색 노선인 것 같은데, 안내판으로 확실히 확인해보세요.

en: Got it. About how long does the walk take?
Maybe five minutes, it's a pretty short walk.
Perfect, thank you so much for your help!
No problem, have a good day!
Hello, thanks for calling. How can I help you?
kr: 안녕하세요, 전화 주셔서 감사합니다. 어떻게 도와드릴까요?

en: Hi, I ordered a pizza an hour ago and it still hasn't arrived.
kr: 안녕하세요, 한 시간 전에 피자를 주문했는데 아직도 도착하지 않았어요.

en: I'm really sorry about that. Could I get your order number, please?
Sure, it's 48291.
Let me check... It looks like the driver got delayed by traffic. It should arrive in 10 minutes.
kr: 확인해볼게요... 기사님이 교통 때문에 지연되신 것 같아요. 10분 안에 도착할 거예요.

en: Ten more minutes? I've already waited an hour, and the food will be cold.
kr: 10분 더요? 벌써 한 시간을 기다렸고, 음식도 식을 텐데요.

en: I completely understand your frustration. I can offer a 50% refund for the inconvenience.
kr: 충분히 이해합니다. 불편을 드린 점에 대해 50% 환불을 해드릴 수 있어요.

en: That would help, thank you. Could you also make sure this doesn't happen next time?
kr: 그렇게 해주시면 도움이 될 것 같아요, 감사합니다. 다음에는 이런 일이 없도록 해주실 수 있나요?

en: Absolutely, I'll add a note to your account. The refund will process within 3 days.
kr: 물론이죠, 계정에 메모해둘게요. 환불은 3일 안에 처리될 거예요.

en: Okay, thank you for resolving this.
